answer.main_body: broken tombstone / stump with fallen piece
answer.evidence: The top fracture/cut surface of the broken stele is clearly depicted in rows 2-7 with a lighter, foreshortened cross-section facing the camera/light source, above the darker vertical south face (rows 8-10). The fallen slab at the bottom also shows 3/4 perspective.
The standing tombstone stump is drawn in pure front elevation with a 1px jagged silhouette along rows 0-2. There is no foreshortened top surface or cut face visible for the top of the column/stele.

answer.main_body: broken tombstone (upright stump with jagged fractured top and fallen slab)
answer.evidence: The upright broken stone clearly shows a fractured top surface across rows 2–7 (about 5 rows of lighter, faceted cross-section) above its darker south face (rows 8–11). The fallen horizontal piece below also shows its top face (rows 11–13) and south face (rows 14–15).

The broken cut/fracture surface of the tombstone is visibly foreshortened and facing the camera from row 1 to row 7 (approx 5 rows of depth) above the south-facing dark stone wall (rows 8-10). The base plinth also clearly shows its horizontal top surface (rows 11-13) above its south face (rows 14-15).
